Improving the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) by Hybrid Approach: An analysis
abstract: <jats:p>Metaheuristics are widely used to address various optimisation problems today. They can yield results with acceptable accuracy when the problem size is large and exact methods become computationally expensive. This work combines the popular Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) in the first phase and an untested updating expression in the second phase to form a hybrid algorithm. The second phase applies the trigonometric "Sine" function over the random numbers generated using Levy Flight Strategy, hence termed as "SineL”, to generate random numbers between [-1, +1] to produce new solutions. 50 benchmarks are used to validate the results of individual GWO, SineL and hybrid algorithm GWO:SineL and simulated for the same number of function evaluations. The overall results prove that the hybrid variant is performing well over the individual GWO and SineL.</jats:p>

title: DLLO:A Learned Join Query Optimizer for Data Lake
abstract: <jats:p>With the rapid development of deep learning, learned query optimizers (LQOs) have emerged as a prominent research hotspot in the database community. However, applying LQOs to data lake environments still faces formidable obstacles: cardinality estimation-based LQOs struggle to accurately model network overhead and cross-node data distribution, while cost model-based LQOs are highly susceptible to cold-start problems and environmental noise. To address these challenges, we design a learned query optimizer framework for Data Lakes (DLLO), whose core is a modular learned join ordering optimizer. To overcome the limited optimization capability of traditional optimizers in complex multi-table joins, DLLO adopts a decoupled design that seamlessly integrates a normalizing flow-based learned cardinality estimator (FACE) and a Tree-LSTM-based reinforcement learning join ordering search model (RTOS). Furthermore, by employing an ``offline pre-training + online fine-tuning&apos;&apos; dual-model coordination mechanism, DLLO effectively mitigates the interference caused by network fluctuations in data lake environments during model training. Tailored to the characteristics of data lakes, we also design a parallelized data preprocessing method for FACE to support efficient training on large-scale data. Experimental results on the JOB benchmark demonstrate that, compared to Spark&apos;s native static optimizer (ROW) and adaptive query execution engine (AQE), DLLO achieves end-to-end query speedups of 1.8 × and 1.7×, respectively.</jats:p>

title: High-Resolution Be Aware: Improving Self-Supervised Real-World Super-Resolution
abstract: <jats:p>Self-supervised learning is crucial for super-resolution (SR) because ground-truthimages are usually unavailable for real-world settings.Existing methods derive self-supervision from low-resolution images by creatingpseudo-pairs or by enforcing a low-resolution reconstruction objective. These methodsstruggle with insufficient modeling of real-world degradations and a lack of knowledgeabout high-resolution imagery, resulting in unnatural super-resolved results. Wepresent a new method to fine-tune off-the-shelf SR models for real-world domains. Ourmethod features a controllable degradation modeling based on the quality of super-resolution results. We also introduce a feature-alignment regularizer that constrains thedistribution of super-resolved images. These novelties strengthen awareness of thehigh-resolution image and improve self-supervision for real-world SR. Experimentsshow that our self-supervised method first produces balanced improvements in fidelityand perception.</jats:p>
